title: Apollo Power Generation Facility
warnings: DO NOT CONFUSE THIS FACILITY WITH THE CITY PLANT FILED ONE DIRECTORY UP. This is Will-Power OH LLC - Apollo, a private 350 MW behind-the-meter generating station at 11902 Middleton Pike in Middleton Township. Ohio EPA facility ID 0387022027. The NPDES records at data/extracted/oepa/bowling-green/2PD00009* are the CITY of Bowling Green's wastewater plant at 901 N. Dunbridge Road. Different operator, different facility, different medium, different permit program — they share only the county and the agency.

THE THREE "MAJOR SOURCE" TESTS SPLIT THREE WAYS HERE AND THE MARGINS ARE THIN. See major_source_status below before describing this plant as major or minor anything. It is a MAJOR source for Title V, NOT major for PSD, and NOT major for MACT — all at once, all correctly.

A COMMENT IS NOT A FINDING. The Response to Comments block below reproduces what members of the public asserted and what Ohio EPA answered. Neither side's assertion is adopted here as fact. Where a response states an agency determination (the single-source determination, the PSD threshold arithmetic), that determination is the agency's and is tagged as such.

title: Bowling Green Water Pollution Control (WPC)
warnings: Table 12's low flows are NOT measured on Poe Ditch, and not measured anywhere near Bowling Green. They are drainage-area-adjusted from USGS gauge 04195500 (Portage River at Woodville) over 1951-97 — a record that closed before the network's own derived 7Q10 window (1980-2024) opens. The footnote is explicit: "Flow data from Low-Flow Characteristics of Stream in Ohio through Water Year 1997 and adjusted for drainage area." Treat the 0.364 cfs as the REGULATORY denominator that this permit's limits were actually computed against, not as a measurement of the ditch, and do not reconcile it against a derived value by preferring one — they are different arithmetic over different records. Same posture as Ottawa (data/extracted/oepa/ottawa/2PD00028.fs.npdes.yaml).

The plant is far larger than the water it discharges into. Table 12 states the discharger flow as 15.47 cfs (10 MGD) against an annual 7Q10 of 0.364 cfs in the same table — a ratio of about 42 to 1. Under design-flow low-flow conditions Poe Ditch below this outfall is effluent, not diluted effluent. This is a [verified] reading of two numbers printed in one table; the ratio itself is arithmetic and is tagged [inference] where it is asserted downstream.

The water quality criteria applied to this discharge are NOT Poe Ditch's own. Poe Ditch is designated Limited Resource Water; the fact sheet states on p. 6 that the criteria associated with the North Branch Portage River's higher uses (Warmwater Habitat, Primary Contact Recreation) "are applied to Bowling Green WPC to be protective of this higher quality stream." A screen that reads Poe Ditch's LRW designation and stops there will apply the wrong criteria.

The total phosphorus limit was NOT tightened by this permit. The reduction from 1.0 to 0.7 mg/L happened in the PRIOR action, permit 2PD00009*SD (p. 9: "the monthly average limit for total phosphorus was reduced from 1.0 to 0.7 mg/L in permit 2PD00009*SD"). This *TD renewal CONTINUES it — "this permit proposes that the same phosphorus limits be continued under the adaptive management approach." Any claim that the 2022 renewal cut the phosphorus limit is wrong; the 2022 renewal declined to cut it further while Ohio EPA waited to resurvey.

The TMDL's own target for this plant is 0.5 mg/L total phosphorus and it was never adopted as a limit. Page 9: the TMDL "assessed multiple scenarios for assigning phosphorus reductions but none resulted in reaching the in-stream target," and it "recommended an implementation strategy ... with a target effluent concentration of 0.5 mg/L for Bowling Green WPC but no formal wasteload allocation was approved." The operative 0.7 mg/L limit rests on best technical judgement, not on an approved WLA.

receiving_water_assessment.recreation_exculpatory: Carried at equal weight, per the discipline: "To reduce bacteria loads to the receiving stream, the City has implemented its Long Term Control Plan to reduce untreated CSO discharges and has had only two violations of the E. coli effluent limits at the treatment facility in the last five years." The E. coli impairment is identified both UPSTREAM and downstream of Poe Ditch, which is not a pattern this outfall alone can produce.
receiving_water_assessment.human_health_impairment: "The human health use in North Branch Portage River is impaired due to high polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) levels found in the tissue of sport fish." No PCB limit or PCB source attribution to this plant appears anywhere in the fact sheet.

As a result, the TMDL recommended an implementation strategy to address the identified nutrient impairment with a target effluent concentration of 0.5 mg/L for Bowling Green WPC but no formal wasteload allocation was approved. Based on best technical judgement and using the TMDL as guidance, the monthly average limit for total phosphorus was reduced from 1.0 to 0.7 mg/L in permit 2PD00009*SD." The *TD renewal continues those limits pending an Ohio EPA resurvey that, as of this fact sheet, had not happened.

title: Bowling Green Water Pollution Control
warnings: THE LIMIT TABLE YOU WANT DEPENDS ON THE DATE. Part I.A carries TWO complete limit tables for the same outfall. Item 1 governs "the period beginning on the effective date of this permit and lasting through the 36th month"; Item 2 governs "the period beginning on 37th month after the effective date of this permit and lasting until the expiration date." The interim table has NO MBAS limit and NO B2EHP limit, and its ammonia limits are looser (winter 7.3/4.8 mg/L, summer 2.7/1.8 mg/L). Reading the final table against a 2023 DMR, or the interim table against a 2026 DMR, produces a wrong answer in both directions.

The permit itself never prints a calendar date for the interim/final changeover — it is expressed only as "the 36th month" and "37th month after the effective date." With an effective date of 2022-05-01 that resolves to on or about 2025-05-01. ICIS-NPDES independently carries the interim limit set as ending 30-APR-25, which agrees. Both are recorded; the arithmetic is [inference] and the ICIS date is [verified] as what the federal system holds. See data/extracted/bowling-green/water-watch.yaml, which turns on this date.

Ambient stations 801 and 901 monitor the NORTH BRANCH PORTAGE RIVER, not Poe Ditch. The permit's own upstream/downstream biology and chemistry are therefore measured a stream removed from the outfall's immediate receptor. Poe Ditch itself is not monitored under this permit at all.
